novelty.justification: The core hypothesis—"safety fine-tuning primarily alters the conditional distribution of the first few response tokens" and is therefore vulnerable once an attacker gets "past the opening tokens"—is essentially the established thesis of Qi et al., “Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep,” rather than a new phenomenon. Searches using “LLM safety alignment few tokens deep,” “prefilling attack alignment depth,” “per-token refusal direction safety,” and “deep refusal token depth training” also identify DeepRefusal (2025), which explicitly addresses insufficient alignment depth by rebuilding refusal mechanisms across token depths, while “Refusal Falls off a Cliff” (2025) already traces refusal signals across token positions mechanistically. The proposed KL depth profile and per-token refusal attribution are natural extensions combining the Qi et al. observation with standard refusal-direction analysis, not a new core relationship, so the limited measurement-level distinction does not rescue the duplicated central hypothesis.
